cards.text: Joshua and Israel have been taking city after city in Canaan. Now, up north, Jabin, king of Hazor, hears about these things. So he sends word to Jobab, king of Madon, and to the kings of Shimron and Achshaph.

And he keeps going: the kings in the mountains, the Arabah, the foothills and the west, plus the Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites, and the Hivites at the foot of Hermon. Friend, Jabin is adding EVERYBODY to the group chat.

cards.question: Jabin's messages go out to the whole north. So these kings came out with all their ___.

cards.text: And they don't come light. It's "a multitude as numerous as the sand on the seashore," with a great number of horses and chariots. I spent years counting dust in a junk drawer, friend, and even I wouldn't try to count THAT.

cards.question: All these northern kings join forces and set up camp to fight against Israel. Where do they camp?
With that huge army camped against Israel, the LORD speaks to Joshua. What's the first thing He tells him?

answers.text: Do not be afraid of them

cards.text: Then the LORD gives a deadline: "for by this time tomorrow I will deliver all of them slain before Israel." Not next year. Not someday. TOMORROW. Friend, I live in a bakery and I can't promise you a batch by tomorrow.

cards.question: The LORD tells Joshua to take the enemy's horses and chariots for Israel's own army.

cards.text: So Joshua doesn't sit and stare at that sea of chariots. By the waters of Merom, he and his whole army come upon them suddenly and attack.

cards.question: Israel wins the battle at Merom because Israel's army is bigger than the northern kings' armies.

cards.text: The LORD delivers them into Israel's hand, and Israel chases them all the way to Greater Sidon and Misrephoth-maim, and east to the Valley of Mizpeh. They strike them down, leaving no survivors.

cards.question: After the battle, Joshua hamstrung the enemy's horses and burned up their chariots. He treated them as the ___ had told him.

cards.text: At that time, Joshua turns back toward Hazor. That's Jabin's city. Yep, Mr. Group Chat himself.

cards.question: Out of all the cities in the north, why does Joshua turn back for Hazor?

answers.text: It had been the head of all these kingdoms
It had the strongest walls in the whole north
It sat the closest to the camp of Israel

cards.text: Joshua captures Hazor, puts its king to the sword, and burns Hazor down. Then he takes all these kings and their cities, as Moses the LORD's servant had commanded.

cards.question: Just like Hazor, Israel burned all the other cities built on their mounds.

cards.text: Israel takes the plunder and livestock of these cities for themselves. But the people are put to the sword, with no one who breathed spared.

cards.question: Joshua leaves nothing undone of all the LORD commanded. The LORD's command reached Joshua through ___.

cards.text: So Joshua takes the whole region: the hill country, the Negev, Goshen, the foothills, the Arabah and the mountains of Israel. From Mount Halak toward Seir all the way to Baal-gad at the foot of Mount Hermon, he captures all their kings.

cards.question: Joshua's war against all these kings was over in just a few days.
Every city in the land was taken in battle except one, which made peace with Israel. Who lived there?

cards.text: The text says it was of the LORD to harden their hearts to engage Israel in battle. That way they would be set apart for destruction and receive no mercy, as the LORD had commanded Moses.
Then Joshua goes after the Anakim in the hill country, a people Moses once called strong and tall (Deuteronomy 9:2). Friend, I'm a stamper on a gold base, so EVERYBODY's tall to me.

cards.question: After Joshua's campaign, no Anakim survived anywhere at all.
Joshua took the entire land, just as the LORD had spoken to Moses. Then he gave it as an ___ to Israel, by the allotments to their tribes.

cards.text: And after all those battles, the chapter ends with one quiet line: "Then the land had rest from war."

findings.problem: The card says Joshua and Israel have been taking city after city in Canaan. That fact comes from Joshua 10, outside the passage, and the card gives it no reference. The card only cites Joshua 11:1.

rule.text: **References.** Every Bible fact he states carries its reference.

findings.problem: Verses 2-3 are a list of places and peoples, which makes them a long stretch. The card names nearly every item: mountains, Arabah, foothills, west, Canaanites, Amorites, Hittites, Perizzites, Jebusites and Hivites at Hermon. It should sum up the list in a few words.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: The joke 'I live in a bakery and I can't promise you a batch by tomorrow' doesn't click. A bakery is exactly the place that can promise a batch by tomorrow, so the comparison leaves the baker asking 'huh?' instead of laughing.

rule.text:
4. It clicks instantly for any adult, with no explaining.
5. If a stranger would say "huh?", rewrite it.

findings.problem: The card says Hazor is Jabin's city. That fact comes from Joshua 11:1, but the card cites only Joshua 11:10.

rule.text: **Cite exactly what the card uses.** Every story card cites the verses it tells, from the first verse it uses to the last, no wider and no narrower.

findings.problem: The card carries more than two beats: Hazor is captured and its king is killed, Hazor is burned, and then all the other kings and cities are taken. It should be split.

rule.text: Aim for one beat per story card. Two is the most. If a story card has more than two things happening, split it.

findings.problem: Card 3 already says Joshua acted 'as Moses the LORD's servant had commanded.' That gives away the answer to this later question, which asks who the LORD's command reached Joshua through (Moses).

rule.text: No card ever gives away the answer to a choice card that comes later.

findings.problem: Verses 16-17 are land boundaries, which makes them a long stretch. The card lists every region and both end points item by item. It should sum up the stretch in a few words.

rule.text: He says in a few words what it covers and doesn't go item by item.

findings.problem: The card says every city was taken in battle 'except one.' The text says no city made peace 'except the Hivites living in Gibeon.' It never says this was a single city, and Joshua 9:17 lists several Gibeonite cities.

rule.text: **Don't stretch the text.** Exaggerate only in his own jokes.

findings.problem: No card ever tells the baker that Anakim survived in Gaza, Gath and Ashdod (Joshua 11:22). The true or false card only shows that the statement is false. Card 11 also leaves out that Joshua devoted the Anakim to destruction along with their cities (11:21). The baker leaves Prep missing these details.

rule.text: When the baker leaves Prep, they understand the whole passage without missing an important detail.

findings.problem: The blank comes right after 'an,' so 'an tribute' is ungrammatical. That rules out the wrong answer 'tribute' and makes the right answer easier to spot.

rule.text: Don't let the right answer stand out. All the answers should sound alike.
